preview.playersNote: Four Hurricanes and five Bearkats who could shape Thursday night.

intro.heading: The matchup
intro.body:
Thursday night is about the district race. **Klein Cain (4–1, 2–1)** walks into Klein Memorial Stadium to face an unbeaten **Klein (6–0, 4–0)** team that just hung **52–0** on Klein Forest. The Bearkats sit tied with Klein Collins atop **District 15-6A**. A Cain win pulls the Hurricanes within a game of the leaders; a Klein win puts the Bearkats alone in first until Collins plays Tomball on Saturday.

The Hurricanes are coming off their roughest half of the season. Last week's **40–24** loss to Collins saw a **24–14** halftime lead dissolve into a **26–0** second half, with two interceptions and no points after the break. The response starts with the run game. **Eyan Johnson (#16)** managed just 19 yards on nine carries against Collins. Cain needs him back in the middle of things Thursday night.

Dave Campbell's Oct 5 Class 6A poll has Klein at **No. 25 (6-0)**, while the Hurricanes, **No. 25** in the Sep 28 poll, fell out after the Collins loss. VYPE's Houston-area 6A poll, published **Oct 4**, has three Klein ISD schools ranked: **Klein Collins** at **No. 14**, **Klein** at **No. 18**, and **Klein Cain** at **No. 25**.

Four teams get in from District 15-6A, and Cain sits third at **2–1** with the head-to-head over Tomball in its pocket. And since Cain's 3,784 students make it the district's largest school, a postseason run goes through **Division I**.

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson managed just 19 yards on nine carries against Collins, his quietest night of the season. The bounce-back spot is obvious: he still leads Cain at 100.4 rushing yards per game with nine total touchdowns, and his 80-yard kickoff return for a score last week was the highlight of the loss. When he gets going early, everything else opens up.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Hanks has thrown eight touchdown passes and run for five more, averaging 85.4 rushing yards a game. His two second-half interceptions helped turn the Collins game; Cain needs a cleaner night from him Thursday. His legs remain Cain's best broken-play weapon, and Klein has to account for him on every snap.

players.name: Cooper Karns
players.copy: Karns leads the Hurricanes at 83.4 receiving yards per game and has been Hanks' most reliable target all season, including six catches for 85 yards against Collins. If Klein loads the box to stop Johnson, the outside throws to Karns become the release valve.

players.name: Jaemin Gilstrap
players.copy: Gilstrap spent plenty of time in Collins' backfield last week, finishing with four tackles and two for loss. Against a Klein offense that wants to stay on schedule, his edge pressure could be Cain's best disruptive force.

players.name: Carter Lattelle
players.copy: Lattelle is the engine of the 6–0 start with 12 touchdown passes, spreading the ball to a deep receiver group. He threw for 126 yards and two scores in the early win over Eisenhower and has kept the Bearkats on schedule all season. Pressure him and the whole offense tightens up.

players.name: Mike Brown
players.copy: Brown is Lattelle's first read and the district's most dangerous receiver at 98.2 yards per game with six touchdowns. His 75-yard catch against Eisenhower showed the home-run speed. Cain's corners have to know where he is on every snap.

players.name: Kendrick Brown
players.copy: Kendrick Brown leads a three-headed Klein ground game at 66.2 yards a contest, with Evan Juniel (39.5) and Bryne Johnson (39.3) rotating behind him. The Bearkats stay ahead of the chains running downhill; fitting the run is job one for Cain's front seven.

players.name: Dolan Guedry
players.copy: Guedry leads the Bearkat defense at 8.0 tackles a game with a sack, the quarterback of a unit that just pitched a 52–0 shutout. He'll be the man assigned to sort out Cain's run-pass conflict all night.

players.name: Cash Hines
players.tag: Klein High spotlight: No. 2 linebacker in 2029 class
players.copy: Klein High School's Aug. 20 spotlight calls Hines the No. 2 linebacker and No. 18 player nationally in the 2029 class, but does not name the ranking service. MaxPreps lists him at 6.8 tackles a game with an interception. The sophomore gives Cain another defender to account for, not just a name on a recruiting list.

items.title: Protect the football
items.body: The Collins loss turned on two second-half interceptions, and Klein's secondary takes it away: **Cash Hines (#5)**, **Dyshon Washington (#26)** and **Ashton Vasser (#24)** each have a pick. Give this offense extra possessions and it scores; give them away and Thursday gets long.

items.title: Get Eyan Johnson going early
items.body: Nineteen yards on nine carries was Johnson's quietest night of the year, and the offense stalled with him. Establish the run and **Jace Hanks (#9)** gets the play-action looks that produced **eight** touchdown passes. Cain needs the run game to look like itself again.

items.title: Make someone besides Mike Brown beat you
items.body: **Carter Lattelle (#12)** looks Brown's way first for a reason: **98.2** yards a game and **six** touchdowns. Cloud the coverage his way, tackle the catch, and force the other Bearkat receivers to win one-on-one.

items.title: Fit the run
items.body: Klein rotates three backs averaging over **40** yards a game behind a line opening holes for a **6–0** team. **Jaemin Gilstrap (#42)** set the edge against Collins; the whole front seven has to do it again or the Bearkats will shorten this game.
